title_he: לְשֵׁם אֲדֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ רַנְּנוּ, הוֹי מַאֲמִינִים
review: The hymn is Philippians 2:9–11 with Ephesians 2:8: 1:1–4 is Phil 2:9 (שֵׁם … מֵעַל כָּל־שֵׁם) with Ps 8:2, 2:1–4 Eph 2:8 with John 5:24 (עָבַר מִן־הַמָּוֶת אֶל־הַחַיִּים), 3:1–4 Col 3:1–2 with Heb 7:26, 4:1–4 Col 1:18, 5:1–4 1 John 2:15–17, and 6:1–4 Rev 22:20.

2:3–4 עָבַרְנוּ … מִן־הַמָּוֶת אֶל־הַחַיִּים — the Arabic قَدِ انْتَقَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَوْتِ لِلْحَيَاه is John 5:24 word for word (מִן־הַמָּוֶת אֶל־הַחַיִּים); the Hebrew restores the verse's prepositions rather than paraphrasing 'we passed from death to life', because the stanza is quoting the Lord's own saying.

4:1 מַקְדִּים לְכָל־אֲשֶׁר לוֹ — the Arabic سَابِقًا كُلَّ ذَوِيهِ is 'preceding all His own'; the Hebrew keeps the participle and the relative clause, so the line still says that He goes before His people, which is the stanza's comfort, and not that He is merely first in rank.

4:2 מַעֲמָד — the Arabic مَقَام is 'a standing, a station'; the biblical מָעֳמָד occurs only in Isa 22:19, and the noun is kept because the line needs the sense of a place assigned, not the modern 'position'.

5:4 הוּא אֶל־הַכָּלָיוֹן — the Arabic إِنَّهُ إِلَى الْفَنَاء is 'it tends to perishing'; the Hebrew keeps the masculine pronoun of the Arabic, which refers back to הָעוֹלָם, and uses כִּלָּיוֹן, the prophetic noun for utter destruction (Isa 10:22–23), so the world's end is judgement and not mere decay.
